summary:
Oops! I'm on Mars — NOVA is an interactive, story-driven educational survival game that combines Mars exploration, space science, and real NASA data. Players take the role of an astronaut who wakes up alone on Mars and must survive for 15 days while waiting for rescue. Throughout the game, players explore a pixel-art environment, manage essential resources such as oxygen, food, and water, restore outpost systems, and complete survival missions.

Our project addresses the challenge of making space science more accessible and engaging through interactive learning. By integrating NASA's DONKI space-weather data, players can learn about solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and solar energetic particles while making decisions about astronaut safety. The game also includes interactive spacesuit training to introduce important astronaut equipment.

Through a combination of storytelling, survival challenges, and scientific information, our project aims to raise awareness of the difficulties astronauts face during space exploration and inspire greater interest in astronomy, space technology, and future Mars missions.
details:
Oops! I'm on Mars — NOVA is an interactive, story-driven educational survival game that allows players to experience the challenges of living on Mars. The game follows an astronaut who wakes up alone on Mars with no memory of her past and must survive for 15 days while waiting for a rescue mission from Earth.

Players explore a pixel-art Martian environment, restore damaged outpost systems, manage essential resources such as oxygen, food, and water, and complete daily missions. The game also includes an AI-themed companion named ORBI, which guides players through survival activities and educational challenges.

One of the main features is the integration of NASA's Space Weather Database of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI). The game uses real NASA records of solar flares (FLR), coronal mass ejections (CME), and solar energetic particle (SEP) events to help players understand space weather and radiation hazards. Players examine NASA observations and make decisions about astronaut safety, including whether to continue outdoor activities or remain inside a radiation shelter. The game also provides an interactive spacesuit assembly activity based on NASA's Extravehicular Mobility Unit (EMU), teaching players the functions of different spacesuit components.

Our project aims to make space science more engaging and accessible by combining scientific information with interactive gameplay. Rather than simply reading about Mars exploration, players can learn through exploration, problem-solving, and decision-making.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with HTML5 Canvas for the 2D game environment, animations, and character movement. NASA's DONKI API and educational resources were incorporated to support the scientific content. The game runs in a web browser without requiring specialized hardware.

What makes our project creative is its combination of a survival storyline, pixel-art exploration, resource management, interactive astronaut training, and real NASA space-weather records. Our team considered scientific accuracy, user experience, accessibility, educational value, and gameplay difficulty when designing the project.

Ultimately, we hope the game will encourage students and space enthusiasts to develop an interest in astronomy, space weather, and the challenges of future human exploration of Mars.
